stores.title: Stores
stores.intro: The group's Shopify stores. Each belongs to one company.
stores.addHelp: Create an app in the Shopify Dev Dashboard, install it on the store and enter its client ID and secret. The secret is stored encrypted and never shown again.
stores.name: Name
stores.codeHint: 2–5 Latin letters/digits. Internal code (lists, rules) — not part of warehouse order ids.
stores.backfillHelp: Imports orders created in the last N days. Read-only towards Shopify.
stores.codGatewaysHint: One per line, exactly as Shopify shows them.
stores.skuPrefixHint: Stripped before matching to master products.
stores.fulfilTriggerHint: With "Accepted by the warehouse" the order is marked fulfilled in Shopify on acceptance (no e-mail to the customer until there is a tracking number); the tracking number and statuses (in transit, delivered, failed) follow. Shopify app scopes needed: write_merchant_managed_fulfillment_orders (fulfilment and tracking) and write_fulfillments (statuses), plus read_orders. If the warehouse cancels an accepted shipment, the Shopify fulfillment stays and a task is opened; a re-sent shipment with the same lines reuses it and updates its tracking.
stores.replaceCredentialsHelp: After a new secret in the Dev Dashboard. The connection is re-tested.

orders.codAmountsNote: The amount the courier collects, in the destination country's local currency — the same as "Expected" in the COD report. Not comparable with "Total of COD orders" (order currency).

shipments.note: Shipments created in the period, by their current status. Sent = has a ship date or status Shipped or later. Delivery rate = delivered / sent; return rate = returned / sent. Cancelled before shipping and failed submissions are excluded from the rates; shipments still on the way count as sent. Shipments cancelled after shipping count as sent but not as in transit. The carrier is the code the warehouse returned (FHB parcel service); euShipments shipments do not store the courier.

timing.chart: Median and p90 per step (all warehouses)
timing.note: Orders placed in the period (not cancelled). Import = first seen in the CRM; approved = first Approved event; submitted, shipped and delivered from the first shipment's dates, else from the order history. A step counts only when both dates exist. Median = half of the orders were faster; p90 = 9 in 10 were faster.
